findings.finding: The no-match required enough religion-specific courses to approximate Groningen's 120-EC disciplinary foundation before accepting any UCR response. That is stricter than the current contract, which permits a coherent related-fields programme when every course makes a concrete contribution and the missing discipline is stated honestly. The selected Groningen route and current programme evidence explicitly organise religion's cultural and political impact through history, art history, philosophy, law, sociology, psychology and political science.
findings.correction: Replace the exception with one complete Religion, cultural heritage & political conflict alternative. Its 23 non-PPD courses form three cumulative strands in religion-related narrative/visual heritage, philosophical inquiry and law/social/political analysis. Preserve explicit gaps in major religious traditions, ritual, sacred-text study and religion-specific methods; retain all corrected comparator components and route evidence unchanged.

findings.finding: Both related-fields alternatives remain coherent and content-supported. The first combines inhabited landscapes, climate adaptation, material/energy life cycles, historical settlements and spatial/computational evidence. The second makes a substantive 30-EC shift from programming, data science, machine learning and optimisation to sociology, civil-society theory, economics and public economics for user needs and shared-environment development. Neither is presented as architectural studio, structural engineering or building physics.
